=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:682 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: OpenRouter API key extraction does not strip surrounding whitespace, so a key containing whitespace may not be redacted from model output.
  WHY: The unstripped environment value will not match model-emitted text containing the key without that whitespace, allowing the raw key to be posted in GitHub comment bodies or issue descriptions.
- scripts/unblock_scan.py:226-230 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The `history_incomplete` branch still uses the old `comment_times` heuristic to decide whether to dispatch.
  WHY: A recently refreshed wait marker outside the visible last-30 comments can be missed, allowing duplicate judge dispatch before the cooldown expires.
- scripts/unblock_scan.py:251 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The `select` return value omits `verify_history`, so the poller never triggers full REST history verification.
  WHY: Candidates with incomplete history that pass the old `comment_times` check can be dispatched without verification.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15973 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The details JSON lacks `comment_count`, and the described full-history REST verification and re-selection flow is absent.
  WHY: Candidates with incomplete comment windows may be dispatched or skipped based on incomplete history.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15989-15994 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The initial select failure has no separate error path for the re-selection step that would follow full-history verification.
  WHY: The reviewer reports this as a completeness gap because the verification path itself is absent.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:16008-16016 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A failed post-verification re-selection returns success without emitting an `UNBLOCK_SCAN` diagnostic line.
  WHY: The workflow log provides no signal that re-selection failed and candidate dispatch was aborted.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:gh_retry gh api --paginate --slurp "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${verify_item}/comments?per_page=100" | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The paginated REST read retrieves every comment for `verify_item` without an upper bound on page count.
  WHY: A high-traffic item can make the read expensive in API calls and wall-clock time, pushing the poller tick toward its 5-minute budget.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_shell_segments_with_operators | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The parser treats any digit-only argument immediately before a redirection operator as a file descriptor, even when whitespace separates them.
  WHY: In `git push origin 2 > /tmp/push.log`, it removes the valid refspec `2`, so `_push_targets` checks the current branch instead and a push to a merged-PR branch named `2` can bypass the guard.
- tests/test_audit_plans_command.py:29-30 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: `test_template_parity` asserts byte equality between `.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` and `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md`, but the files differ.
  WHY: The test fails with an `AssertionError`, causing `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` and the aggregate `lint` check to fail.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:103, 126-127 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The root command retains old in-session wording while `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` uses Claude-engine orchestrator hand-off wording.
  WHY: The files fail the byte-for-byte template parity test, causing the required `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` check to fail and blocking PR merge authorization.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]

  expected_change_site: tests/test_unblock_judge.py (test already exists)

  expected_change_site: scripts/unblock_actions.py and scripts/unblock_judge.sh

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:682 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The OpenRouter API key extraction does not strip surrounding whitespace; a key set with leading/trailing whitespace will not match the key embedded in model output text, so the raw key can be posted in GitHub comment bodies or issue descriptions.
  WHY: `os.environ.get("OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "").replace(...)` on an unstripped key does not match model-emitted text that lacks the same whitespace.
- scripts/unblock_scan.py:226-230 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `history_incomplete` branch still uses the old `comment_times` heuristic, which allows dispatch when any comment in the visible 30-message window is older than the marker cooldown period, even though an even older wait marker refreshed in place outside the visible window could still be active.
  WHY: A recently refreshed wait marker outside the creation-ordered last-30 comments appears absent, allowing a duplicate judge dispatch before the cooldown expires.
- scripts/unblock_scan.py:251 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `select` function return value does not include `verify_history`, so the poller's `jq -r '.verify_history // empty'` always evaluates to empty and never triggers a full REST history verification. Incomplete-history candidates that pass the old `comment_times` check are dispatched without verification.
  WHY: The poller reads `.verify_history` to know which candidate needs full-history checking; without this field, no REST verification ever runs.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15973 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The details JSON lacks the `comment_count` field needed to verify that a paginated REST read captured all comments. The `history_incomplete` flag exists but there is no actual REST verification flow (no `verify_item`, no `full_comments.json`, no re-selection after verification).
  WHY: Without the full-history REST verification path, candidates with incomplete 30-comment windows are either dispatched (if `comment_times` permits) or skipped (if `history_incomplete` blocks) based on an incomplete view of their comment history.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15989-15994 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: When `scripts/unblock_scan.py select` exits non-zero, the function logs `outcome=skip reason=select_failed` and returns. There is no separate error path for the re-selection step that would follow full-history verification. Since that re-selection path also does not exist, this is a completeness gap rather than a runtime defect in the current code.
  WHY: Currently no issue since the verification path itself is absent.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Safety. Model-written text never starts a comment line, because the poller's `/judge_resume`, `/revalidate` and `/re-security-pass` handlers match a command at the start of any line. Tests cover this." (from PR description)
  Expected change site: tests/test_unblock_judge.py (test already exists)
  Evidence of absence: The test `test_model_text_never_starts_a_command_line` is present and covers both issue and PR contexts with COMMAND_LINE regex validation. Requirement is satisfied.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 1
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "the poller's `/judge_resume`, `/revalidate` and `/re-security-pass` handlers match a command at the start of any line" (PR description)
  Expected change site: scripts/unblock_actions.py and scripts/unblock_judge.sh
  Evidence of absence: Verified that `_fixup_body` and `reset_ops` do NOT put model text before command words in comment bodies; the model-text `instructions` field follows `Change: ` prefix, not a leading line position. Requirement is satisfied.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 1
- NOTE ON PRE-EXISTING CI FAILURE: The `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` CI job fails because `.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` (root) does not match `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` byte-for-byte — the root file retains pre-Phase-2 in-session wording while the template has been updated with orchestrator hand-off wording (lines 1, 7, 29, 32, 42, 103, 126-127). This file is NOT in the PR's changed files and the failure is pre-existing on the base branch. This causes the aggregate `lint` check to also fail.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- tests/test_audit_plans_command.py:29-30 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The required CI check tests-hooks-and-orchestrator fails because test_template_parity asserts byte equality between .claude/commands/audit-plans.md and workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md. Lines 103, 126, and 127 in workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md contain Phase 6 orchestrator hand-off phrasing ("Claude-engine orchestrator hand-off" and "legacy /implement-plan-claude") while .claude/commands/audit-plans.md retains the legacy in-session phrasing ("(in-session)", "Claude implements it in-session", and "in-flight /implement-plan-claude").
  WHY: test_template_parity fails with an AssertionError, causing tests-hooks-and-orchestrator to exit with code 1. As recorded in the check-run logs for head commit 6593bf59d73af8f777706de6f0cf30ebbe2b718a, this causes the aggregate CI check lint to fail and blocks PR merge authorization.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:16008-16016 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: In run_unblock_scan, the reselection call executed after comment history verification runs `selection="$(PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 scripts/unblock_scan.py select ...)" || return 0`. The initial select call at line 15991 logs UNBLOCK_SCAN candidates=${count} outcome=skip reason=select_failed on non-zero exit, but the reselection step returns 0 silently without emitting any UNBLOCK_SCAN log line.
  WHY: If the reselection command fails due to unparseable JSON or an unhandled exception, run_unblock_scan terminates immediately without writing an UNBLOCK
